title: Father's barbershop and the Brotherhood Eyes gossip sheet
summary: His father's Gretna barbershop drew men from Sam Peet's ballroom, and Tex recalls the gossip paper Brotherhood Eyes.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you follow the wolves as a child, as a kid?

No, I would just see them marching. But see, now, when I moved on this side of the river and I went into the service, I lost contact with the wolves organization. Not that I was a member or anything, but my father knew a lot of the people who were members of the wolves, because from time to time, some of the members would come to his barbershop. See, my father being a barber, well, he had a barbershop on Wire Street in Gretchen. And a lot of times, and see, the reason why a lot of people would come to the barbershop, because there was a fellow by the name of Sam Peet, who had a ballroom right on the corner. And when they didn't feel like drinking or stopped drinking, they would come. See, my father had a ceiling fan. That was before air conditioning. They used to come to the barbershop to cool off. My father had what you call it, isolating fans. Yeah, fans.
Yeah, but the barbershops in general tend to attract people who aren't doing anything.
Who are just kind of hanging out.

That's where you get a lot of conversation. Right. And you learn a lot of things about the neighborhood. Yeah, oh, yeah. And what went on and so forth and so on. We're talking about gossip. Oh, yeah. And incidentally, I never forget, they had a fellow by the name of Freddie Craft over in Gretchen. He used to... He was the circulation representative for the Brotherhood Eyes. Some of the greatest journalistic writing I have ever seen in my life was in the Brotherhood Eyes. But there was slam-bass people about Professor So-and-So was seen hanging out with Sister Sadie G and things like that. And old left-handed Ike Rod Dixon was seen in the alley with fancy doing the fanning, things like that. One of these good days, boy, I'll show you some copies I have. My mother used to keep all of those things, so I got them.
But this was all barbershop gossip or street copy?

Well, no, no, wait, now, the Brotherhood Eyes came out of Dallas, Texas around about 1932 or 1933. But they hired people in and around the New Orleans and Gretchen area to pick up the gossip for them. But now here's what happened. They went out of business because somebody sued the company. And they went out of business, but I tell you, it was some of the greatest journalistic writing I'd ever seen.
